ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10618, as amended); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Act No. 5493, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information; Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 586, governing Yuhan Hoesa; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulations on beneficial owner identification; and Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules requiring identity and register documentation for founding members, directors, and authorized representatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign corporate founding member and ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, tax authority, or official corporate registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Hague Apostille Convention states: notary authentication followed by Apostille issued by the designated competent authority; use Path A exclusively and do not add Korean consular legalization. Path B for non-member states: notary authentication, then authentication by the country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; use Path B exclusively and do not add Apostille. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company register or registered-office authority of the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all members, directors, UBOs and signatories before onboarding and a second time before disbursement: against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) sanctions and PEP database, UN Security Council sanctions (including 1718 DPRK and global terrorism designations), US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (including the 50-percent ownership rule), FATF public statements, and Korean domestic investigative and financial police lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, politically exposed family members, and close associates; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence must be collected and refreshed quarterly if film financing is involved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea; official name search and provisional trade-name registration service at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be entered in Korean script or as a Korean phonetic transliteration of a foreign corporate name; a foreign-language equivalent may be carried supplementary in English but does not serve as the registered name. The four-tier screening is: (1) exact Hangul match; (2) phonetic transliteration equivalence; (3) conflict against registered names and well-known trade names in the same registry district; and (4) inclusion of the mandatory statutory suffix Yuhan Hoesa and descriptive elements that do not mislead the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days after a formal rejection, file a written statement of objection with the same court registry, including the proposed name, the registry reference, the relevant Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Rule, and the factual basis for why the name is distinct and not misleading. The registry official must issue a written decision; if the objection is dismissed, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. An extension of provisional trade-name registration must be requested before expiry; if extension is refused, a fresh application may be filed immediately while preserving priority only if no conflicting registration has intervened.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office may be a physical office, studio, or serviced office in Korea; a pure virtual office providing only a mailbox is formally possible for court registration, but Korean banks applying the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality will reject it for corporate account opening,

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea, as enacted in the Korean Commercial Code (Law No. 6916, consolidated), specifically Articles 169 through 209 for companies generally and Articles 287-7 through 309 for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company); relevant incorporation sections include Articles 287-20, 290, 292, 301, 306 and 407 concerning articles of incorporation, paid-in capital, statutory officers, and registration of establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, operated through the Supreme Court of Korea's CourtNet electronic commercial registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa, executed by all incorporators and notarized, submitted together with the Registration Application for Establishment of a Limited Liability Company and all statutory attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korean law sets no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa, and the capital amount is determined solely by the Articles of Incorporation. However, the full declared paid-in capital must be deposited into a domestic Korean bank escrow account prior to court registration, the bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit in the name of the company, and the funds must remain blocked and unavailable for withdrawal until the court-issued incorporation registration certificate has been obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This Pro-Forma First Board Resolution of Yuhan Hoesa is adopted by the incorporators and initial shareholders acting in accordance with the Commercial Act of South Korea. Whereas the subscribed capital has been fully paid into the company's domestic escrow account and all statutory pre-incorporation conditions have been satisfied, it is hereby resolved by unanimous written consent of the incorporators as follows. First, the paid-in capital of the company, in the amount declared in Article 2 of the Articles of Incorporation, is deemed fully subscribed, issued, and allocated to the subscribing shareholders in the amounts and share classes set out in the subscriber ledger, and the board ratifies the issuance of shares to the founding shareholders. Second, the board adopts the Articles of Incorporation as the company's organic law and confirms that the registered office is located at the address listed in the incorporation registration; the board authorizes the representative director and any attorney-in-fact to execute, file, and record the incorporation with the competent Commercial Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court and to make any non-substantive amendments required by that registry. Third, a banking resolution is established: the board designates the domestic bank chosen by the incorporators as the principal banker, opens the corporate settlement account, and authorizes the representative director and any one jointly designated officer to execute SWIFT wire transfers and Wise B2B foreign payment rail instructions for the legitimate receipt of animation production proceeds. Fourth, the statutory officers are appointed as follows: one representative director who shall also hold the office of Chief Executive Officer; one inside director; and one statutory auditor, unless the company qualifies for the statutory audit exemption available to small limited liability companies under the Commercial Act. Each officer shall hold office until the next annual shareholders' meeting and may be re-appointed. Fifth, the officers are expressly authorized to prepare and file corporate tax registration, value-added tax registration, business permit filings, foreign exchange reports, and all ancillary declarations necessary to give effect to this resolution. This resolution takes effect immediately upon adoption and supersedes all prior oral or written understandings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Dossier Assembly and Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Registry Office, Korean CourtNet Electronic Commercial Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel must first search the proposed corporate name on the CourtNet portal to verify that no identical or confusingly similar limited liability company exists within the same registration branch. After the name search is confirmed, counsel must collect the passport or alien registration card of every incorporator, obtain an apostilled certificate of good standing for any foreign corporate incorporator, and arrange certified Korean translation of every non-English corporate record. The draft Articles of Incorporation must be printed on plain A4 paper, paginated, and bound in two identical original dossier sets. Counsel must also prepare a table of statutory registration attachments matching the CourtNet submission requirements so that no document is missing at filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or alien registration card of each incorporator
Apostilled certificate of good standing for any corporate incorporator
Certified Korean translation of all non-English records
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean statutory format
Name search confirmation from CourtNet
Power of attorney if counsel will execute on behalf of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity to an existing company, counsel shall immediately file a correction with a second available name; if a suspension is issued, counsel submits an explanatory brief and certified prior-use evidence within the CourtNet review window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Execution by Incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean certified notary public, or the court attorney-notarization section of the local district court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators, or their duly appointed attorneys-in-fact acting under a notarized power of attorney, must appear before a Korean notary public. The notary verifies identity, confirms legal capacity, reads the final provisions, and witnesses execution by signature or corporate seal. If any incorporator resides abroad, execution may occur before a Korean consulate or before a foreign notary with apostille, followed by sworn Korean translation. The notary then issues a notarial certificate and returns one original docket to the company. Any subsequent substantive amendment to the Articles after notarization invalidates the notarial certificate and requires renewed execution.
required_dossiers: Original draft Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of all incorporators
Power of attorney if an agent signs
Notarized consent of each proposed director and auditor
Apostille or consular legalization for foreign signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to authenticate due to an inconsistency, counsel reconciles the text with the final registered office details and re-executes before the same notary within three business days; if a foreign signature is questioned, counsel provides supplementary apostille evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic Korean commercial bank maintaining new-company escrow accounts, including Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, or IBK branches
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the company director must open a temporary restricted escrow account at a domestic Korean bank using the corporate preliminary registration number, and deposit the full declared paid-in capital by wire transfer from the incorporators' individual accounts. The bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit in the name of Yuhan Hoesa stating the amount, date, account number, and confirmation that withdrawals are blocked until presentation of the court-issued corporate registration certificate. All remittances must identify the company name as the remittance reference. The deposit certificate must be dated no more than five business days before the court submission date.
required_dossiers: Preliminary registration number certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Unrestricted outgoing wire instructions from each incorporator
Compliance declaration for Korean foreign exchange and anti-money-laundering review
Certificate of capital deposit from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries mixed deposits, counsel provides a sworn remittance ledger and a unified capital contribution declaration signed by all incorporators, then obtains a replacement deposit certificate correcting the remittance references.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration Filing and Court Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court, Commercial Registration Division, through the Korean CourtNet electronic registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Registration counsel must file the incorporation case on Korean CourtNet by selecting limited liability company incorporation registration for a Seoul-registered entity. The filing docket must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, notarized appointment consents of directors and any auditor, the registered office lease abstract with owner consent, and the identity documents of all initial shareholders. Counsel must simultaneously pay the court registration tax, local educational surtax, and court user fee using the electronic payment module. The court performs a formal legality review and, if no defects exist, issues the certificate of incorporation registration, the corporate seal certificate, and the assigned statutory corporate registration number.
required_dossiers: Fully executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate from the escrow bank
Consent forms of directors and auditor
Registered office lease agreement and owner consent
Power of attorney for registration counsel
Court fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CourtNet issues a defect notice, each defect must be cured online within ten days; if the court suspends registration, counsel files a written statutory reply and pays any additional fee before the peremptory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance and Business License Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district office for the registered office address, National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after receipt of the court registration certificate, the company must file the corporate arrival report with the National Tax Service district office covering the registered office address, applying for a corporate tax identification number and the value-added tax business registration certificate. The same docket is used to open payroll withholding accounts for resident and non-resident officers and to enroll every statutory officer and employee in the mandatory social insurance systems. After approval, the National Tax Service issues the corporate business registration certificate, which is used to open final operating accounts at the settlement bank and to execute commercial agreements with animation and VFX clients.
required_dossiers: Court-issued incorporation registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Power of attorney for tax counsel
Lease agreement and ownership or floor plan proof of registered office
Passport or alien registration card of the representative director
Certified translation of shareholders' foreign corporate resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service rejects the application for incomplete address proof, counsel submits the lease certificate and building floor plan; if social insurance notices show an underpayment, payroll declarations are reissued and a payment plan is requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking Payment Rails and Optional Content Compliance Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign exchange bank chosen for SWIFT wire and Wise B2B settlement, and Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for optional video content distribution notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the tax registration is complete, the representative director must open final commercial settlement accounts at the chosen foreign exchange bank, notify the bank of the Wise B2B and SWIFT wire payment rails, and execute the foreign exchange transaction agreement required for inbound USD and KRW conversion. If the company acts as a direct-to-consumer distributor or cinema exhibitor of its animation content, a separate voluntary content business notification must be filed with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; for pure business-to-business CGI and 3D animation studio production, no statutory industrial license is required. The payment rails must remain consistent with the low-risk anti-money-laundering classification declared by the compliance officer.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Corporate seal certificate and power of attorney for bank signatories
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and payment rails
Foreign transaction identification and AML declarations
Client invoices or purchase orders demonstrating production services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or regulator challenges the payment rail as requiring a prior foreign exchange declaration, counsel files a voluntary foreign exchange report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act or provides evidence of an approved inbound remittance structure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for ISIC 5911 commercial 3D animation as a digital production service; if physical film or animation production stages with large-scale lighting or generator equipment were later introduced, the municipal industry licensing agency of the Seoul Metropolitan Government would become the competent authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; statutory video business licensing does not apply because the entity delivers contracted CGI, VFX and 3D animation assets rather than operating cinema exhibition or broadcasting facilities. The only mandatory operating document is the corporate business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service for corporate tax and value-added tax purposes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - digital service with no industrial installation, no chemical process, no onsite manufacturing, and no environmental impact assessment triggering activity under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; zero onsite wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. If a server rendering farm or data center exceeding 100 kilowatts is installed in the future, the company would be required to report greenhouse gas and electricity consumption data under the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable; the leased office must hold a valid fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire district of the National Fire Agency. No workplace structural load approval is required because there is no heavy industrial equipment. If a rendering server room is installed, the company should obtain an electrical load inspection and seismic secondary-fixation certification from a licensed electrical engineer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs export declarations are filed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa (domestic limited liability company), apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office, or through the HomeTax portal using the corporate Digital Certificate, within 20 days after business commencement. The BRN is simultaneously the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and the Value-Added Tax (VAT) registration number. Required documents include: certificate of incorporation and certified Korean translation; articles of incorporation; board resolution appointing the representative (and, where required, the tax representative); power of attorney; evidence of domestic place of business (lease agreement or certificate of office occupancy); foreign business registration certificate or equivalent; and identity documentation of the appointed representative/shareholders. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business, the entity must appoint a tax representative under the Act on the Coordination of Tax and International Transactions and file the same BRN application before making taxable supplies in Korea; the tax representative submits the application via HomeTax on behalf of the foreign entity. Where the foreign entity only supplies services to Korean business customers in respect of which Korea imposes reverse-charge VAT, registration is ordinarily not required; however, a foreign supplier of digital/electronic services to Korean non-business consumers is required to register under the simplified VAT registration for foreign electronic service suppliers and discharge VAT through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or entity classification election; a Yuhan Hoesa is automatically treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch or pass-through election is available. Corporate tax consolidation under the Corporate Income Tax Act may be elected only by a qualifying parent company controlling 100% of domestic subsidiaries, but it does not alter the entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold. VAT registration is mandatory upon commencement of any business making taxable supplies in Korea, regardless of revenue. Simplified taxable person status is limited to individual sole proprietors whose prior-year taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000; a corporate entity, including a Yuhan Hoesa, is always an ordinary VAT taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B supplies must be evidenced by a tax invoice issued in accordance with the VAT Act. Electronic tax invoices (ETI) are mandatory for all VAT-registered business operators, and each ETI must be transmitted to NTS through HomeTax. ETIs are submitted in structured XML form; high-volume taxpayers may integrate accounting or ERP systems with the HomeTax EDI/API interface. NTS validates and cross-matches buyer and seller ETI data; there is no fiscal digital stamping or real-time pre-clearance denial mechanism. Late submission, non-submission, or submission of false ETI data triggers VAT Act penalty taxes and administrative surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the zero rate applies to exports of goods, supplies of services to foreign countries, and other supplies of goods or services prescribed by Presidential Decree as foreign currency earning activities. For a Korean 3D animation/VFX production company, services to non-resident clients will qualify as zero-rated service exports when the contract is with a non-resident, the consideration is paid in foreign currency, and the services are materially performed for the foreign client's use or exploitation outside Korea, including delivery of animation/CGI files or digital broadcast/streaming content to an overseas buyer. The claim must be substantiated by retaining contractual, payment, and work-product delivery evidence; no domestic VAT is chargeable on qualifying zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS export declaration certificate (Export Declaration Acceptance/Number) issued by Korea Customs Service for physical goods exported from Korea
Commercial invoice issued by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa to the non-resident buyer
Packing list and transport document (bill of lading, air waybill, or international courier delivery record) showing the goods left Korea

Bank-issued Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance/Receipt Certificate or foreign exchange purchase receipt from a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing settlement of export proceeds in foreign currency

Original service/export contract with the non-resident client, delivery acceptance record, and digital file transfer logs for services and digital animation deliverables; a customs export declaration is not required for pure service exports, but the export service documentation bundle must evidence the foreign recipient and foreign use
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice (export tax invoice) issued through HomeTax with the statutory zero-rating exemption code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match zero-rating claims with export declarations, transport documents, foreign exchange settlement receipts, and the relationship between the Korean supplier and the foreign client. If export zero-rating is claimed without lawful substantiation, or if export proceeds are not received in foreign currency within the statutory settlement period, NTS can reverse the zero rate, assess VAT at 10% on the supply value, add statutory penalty taxes (including understatement penalties for unpaid or underpaid VAT and penalties for unissued or false tax invoices), and charge statutory interest. For fraudulent claims, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose criminal fines of up to three times the evaded tax or imprisonment, and the assessment limitation period extends to 10 years where fraud or dishonest concealment is shown.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a regulated but broadly convertible foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercising supervisory authority. Current account transactions, including trade in services, royalties, animation production fees, and ordinary profit remittances, are generally classified as freely convertible and may proceed through authorized foreign exchange banks subject to documentary verification and submission of prescribed foreign exchange reports. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections and external borrowings, are not fully liberalized and require notification, registration, or prior approval depending on the transaction type. Export proceeds are not forcibly surrendered to the central bank, but exporters must ensure that foreign currency receipts are collected within statutory periods, properly received through domestic banks, and recorded for customs and tax reconciliation. Profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is permissible after satisfaction of corporate income tax, tax clearance certification, and submission of board resolutions, financial statements, and auditor confirmations where applicable. Practical hurdles arise from stringent anti-money laundering documentation requirements, the need for foreign exchange transaction reports, and the necessity to evidence the commercial substance of cross-border service transactions involving intangible digital assets such as 3D animation and VFX deliverables. Korean authorities scrutinize mis-invoicing, round-tripping, and shell-company structures, requiring treasury officers to maintain complete underlying contracts and settlement evidence. Overall, Korean won is convertible for operating business transactions, but treasury planning must incorporate reporting lead times and bank-level compliance gates for capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters must collect export proceeds within 6 months from the date of export or the date of loading, unless an extension is approved by the governing foreign exchange bank. Korea does not presently impose a mandatory conversion ratio requiring surrender of export receipts into Korean won; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts, but the receipt must be reported through an authorized domestic foreign exchange bank and trade settlement documentation must evidence the underlying export transaction. Delayed collection, shortfall, or substitution with alternative payment methods requires submission of a written explanation and supporting shipping documents to the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Currency Account and Cross-Border Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low Direct Legal Viability: South Korean law does not classify foreign digital EMI platforms such as Wise or Revolut as authorized banks or licensed domestic money service businesses eligible to provide payment accounts and FX settlement services to a resident Yuhan Hoesa entity. Foreign EMIs are not supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service for domestic account holding and cannot independently supply Korean won clearing, FX purpose code reporting, or export proceeds collection confirmation. They may be used only as supplementary payment origination rails for low-value non-regulated disbursements, but the primary treasury relationship must reside with a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank to satisfy the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and AML KYC obligations. Any arrangement presenting a foreign EMI as the main clearing channel would be structurally non-compliant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks require statutory directors and authorized signatories to undergo face-to-face customer due diligence for corporate account onboarding. In practice, at least one director or designated finance officer must attend in-branch with a passport, certificate of corporate existence, corporate seal certificate, and board resolution authorizing the account opening. Remote opening is not a standard entitlement for a newly established foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa; some banks permit a remote video interview only where the company already has an operating office and the UBO has completed an initial in-branch consultation. Consular proxy opening, using a notarized power of attorney executed at a Korean embassy or consulate, is recognized by certain Tier-1 banks but still requires the authorized proxy to appear in person at the branch to present identification and original notarial documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner ownership chain opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and apostilled corporate register extract of the Yuhan Hoesa, a complete shareholding ledger from incorporation, a UBO declaration form naming every direct and indirect owner above 25%, passport copies of all natural-person owners, a narrative source-of-funds letter, and bank statements covering the capital injection period to prove the provenance of contributed funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and adverse media screening hits on foreign shareholders or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver enhanced due diligence reports from a recognized screening provider covering OFAC, EU, UN, and Korean FSS sanctions lists, PEP status explanations with supporting public records, independent negative media search results, and a corporate governance statement explaining the commercial rationale for each non-resident shareholder and the animation production business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible cross-border service exports flagged as potential false invoicing or transfer mispricing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed client contracts and scope-of-work schedules for commercial 3D animation, itemized invoices, delivery receipts, asset transfer logs, render farm utilization reports, and historical settlement records with prior clients to evidence genuine service delivery and arm's-length pricing for VFX and CGI production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical operating substance and low salary/tax filing history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Korean office lease agreement, studio equipment inventory, employee payroll records and national pension receipts, value-added tax filings, corporate income tax preliminary returns, and a description of production workflow from storyboard through final render to demonstrate that the entity is not a shell used for regulatory arbitrage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity investments from non-resident shareholders must be routed through a SWIFT MT103 wire to a domestic Tier-1 bank account referencing the foreign direct investment notification or registration issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remittance should carry a clear payment narrative such as 'Paid-in capital for Yuhan Hoesa investment' and the appropriate bank code for capital receipts. After the funds arrive, the receiving bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase confirmation and the company must obtain a capital verification or investment certificate from the bank or a certified public accountant before remitting any dividends. All capital proceeds should be held in a dedicated capital escrow account and reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or delegated institution through the bank's e-reporting portal; failure to register the investment and prove the domestic bank settlement channel may block future profit repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service-related disbursements for animation subcontracting, software licensing, render farm fees, and international talent payments may be cleared via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for non-urgent settlements, documentary collections for consignment-based licensing distributions, or commercial letters of credit when a seller requires a bank payment undertaking for large-scale VFX production milestones. Each outward remittance must be supported by the underlying contract, supplier invoice, customs or intellectual property evidence, and a foreign exchange disposition report filed through the domestic bank. For recurring outbound payments to overseas contractors, the treasury should establish a dedicated disbursement account under the same bank relationship to achieve faster internal clearing and to aggregate FX purpose codes for compliance reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forward contracts for hedging real current account exposures such as invoiced animation production fees and royalties
Cross-currency swaps between Korean won and US dollars where the underlying cash flows arise from committed capital or trade settlement obligations
Non-deliverable forward transactions in the offshore NDF market restricted to firms with verifiable underlying won exposures and approved by the domestic foreign exchange bank
Currency options for risk mitigation on large one-off VFX licensing payments, provided the notional amount matches booked receivables or payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Status Consistency Verification and Commercial Registry Amendment Filing (if registered details have changed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry Court of the local district court and National Tax Service for business-registration changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Changes to registered office, directors, members, capital, articles of incorporation or business status must be filed with the commercial registry within 30 days of the change. The annual review should be completed by March 31 to align with the corporate tax filing and general meeting cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration of changes carries commercial registration penalty surcharges, daily delinquency fines for repeated failure, and refusal to register substantive resolutions until prior outstanding filings are cured. Misstated public records can be treated as an administrative offense and may form grounds for the court to appoint an inspector or to dissolve the company if the public records become materially misleading.}],

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Corporations (Oegamusa Beop) and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified public accountant audit is compulsory for a fiscal year if the company meets any of the following quantitative thresholds: (1) total assets on the balance sheet as of year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9 million); (2) total assets are between KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.3 million) and KRW 12 billion and the company meets any of: (a) a total liabilities to total equity ratio above 300%, meaning total liabilities exceed 75% of total assets; (b) annual operating revenue of KRW 50 billion or more (approx. USD 37 million); or (c) an average annual headcount of 300 employees or more; (3) the entity is listed, financial, public, or specially designated as an audit-mandated company under the Act irrespective of size; or (4) any member holding not less than 3% of membership interests requests an audit under the statutory members’ rights procedure. For a Yuhan Hoesa operating a CGI/3D animation studio, the audit trigger is almost always balance-sheet asset size or revenue, not a specific industry license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), which materially aligns with IFRS, is mandatory for entities subject to mandatory external audit, listed companies and financial institutions. Non-listed non-financial companies may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or, for small and medium-size entities, the Korean SME Accounting Standards (K-SME); the selected framework must be applied consistently and the external auditor must issue the report in accordance with Korean standards on auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a stand-alone annual beneficial-ownership filing to a companies registry. The statutory member register is the authoritative ownership record and must be current at all times. For a Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident members, any transfer of membership interests triggers a Foreign Investment Promotion Act change report to KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of the transfer. Domestically, share or membership transfers are evidenced by updating the member register; if the articles of incorporation are amended, the amendment must be registered with the Commercial Registry Court. Financial institutions providing the company’s payment rails (including Wise B2B and Swift wire accounts) are legally obliged under Korean AML/CFT and FATF standards to require a beneficial-owner certification at account onboarding and whenever there is a material ownership change; the company must therefore issue updated UBO confirmations to its banks and tax representatives no later than the annual financial-statement approval date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors (if an auditor is appointed)
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board/Management Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 for a Korean registered address and corporate secretarial/registered agent service in Seoul or Incheon; USD 500 - USD 1,500 for a virtual office or outside the capital region

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top marginal corporate income tax rate; plus 10% local income tax surtax for a combined 26.4% top marginal rate. Lower brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying SME and venture 3D animation/VFX studios may claim R&D tax credits and content-industry investment credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law (up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D expenditures for SMEs depending on the credit-rate formula); no general patent box is available in Korea; free-zone incentives are not assumed; the 10% local income tax surtax applies on the national corporate tax amount after credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NTS HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr) - Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Korean domestic legal form: payout of corporate income tax standard return and tax amount return; Form 27-1 series)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual interim prepayment returns are also required, together with monthly non-resident withholding tax returns for dividends, interest, royalties and service fees paid abroad.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within three months after the end of the fiscal year; a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa must file by 31 March of the following year. Interim prepayment returns are due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year; any tax due is payable by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification, Tax Period and Non-Resident Ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The header section records the company legal name, business registration number, head office address, representative director, fiscal year, industry code (ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110), entity classification as a Korean resident corporation and the identity of all shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick and declare whether the company is a Korean tax resident. List every non-resident shareholder with country of residence, tax identification number and shareholding percentage. If non-resident directors exercise central management and control from Korea, the company remains fully taxable in Korea; if operations are managed abroad, the company must still demonstrate that a Yuhan Hoesa registered in Korea has sufficient board oversight in Korea to avoid a foreign place of effective management challenge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Restated Financial Statements Income (Gross Revenue, Costs and Operating Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the pre-tax book income after applying K-IFRS or K-GAAP, including revenue from 3D animation production contracts, licensing of animation IP, VFX service fees, overseas distribution cash receipts, and all deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all foreign currency revenue into KRW using the Bank of Korea base rate at the transaction date and the closing rate for receivables. Any advance payments for animation services received via Wise B2B or SWIFT wire must be deferred until the performance obligation is satisfied; no foreign-earned revenue may be omitted by claiming a foreign bank account or nominee ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Adjustment Schedule (Additions and Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book income to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses and statutory disallowances and by deducting non-taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties, including management fees, IP royalties and VFX subcontracting fees, are deductible only when supported by valid written contracts, actual services rendered, and full evidence that non-resident withholding tax was paid. The NTS will deny deductions for artificial offshore invoice factories; the company must apply the arm's length standard to every cross-border controlled transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Loss Carryforward Deduction and Reconciled Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the adjusted income after applying unabsorbed prior-year operating losses and any loss carryforward elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the portion of losses already reflected in accepted prior-year returns may be deducted; losses are available for ten years and, for qualifying SMEs, may be carried forward fifteen years. If the Yuhan Hoesa also operates a foreign permanent establishment, in-bound overseas losses must be examined carefully under the applicable tax treaty and foreign tax credit limitation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Base Computation and National Corporate Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the progressive national corporate tax on the taxable income determined in Box 4 and apply the statutory rates to each bracket.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, 21% and 24% national tax brackets correctly. The local income tax surtax is separately reported in Box 6 but is calculated as 10% of the national corporate income tax after all credits. For non-resident shareholders, the company should simultaneously track the distributable earnings that will later give rise to dividend withholding tax when repatriated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits, Incentives, Foreign Tax Credit and Local Income Tax Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim all eligible tax credits from the annual tax base: R&D credits, SME venture credits, job creation credits, foreign tax credits, and other special tax exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For international profit repatriation, the Korean payer must not claim a domestic deduction for dividends distributed; dividends are paid out of after-tax retained earnings. If a foreign tax credit is claimed, the payer must file full evidence of the foreign withholding tax, and any reduction under a double tax treaty must be reconciled with the beneficial ownership and residency certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Interim Prepaid Corporate Tax and Advance Withholding Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct interim corporate tax prepayments, employer tax withholdings, and all previous tax payments made during the business year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all foreign-source tax withholding credits, Korean source WHT already paid on payments to non-residents, and local income tax installments. If the company receives dividends, interest, or royalties from abroad, repatriated amounts are included in income and foreign withholding is credited; the mere routing of payments through foreign digital banks does not alter Korean source taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Final Tax Payable or Refund, Director Declaration and Attached Documents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute final national tax and local income tax surtax due, or calculate refund, and attach audited or compiled financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, transfer pricing disclosures, and treaty relief forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the contemporaneous Local File and Master File if the applicable KRW thresholds are reached, together with any CbC Report notifications. Attach tax residency certificates and beneficial ownership statements for any DTA-reduced withholding on outbound dividends, interest or royalties. The director's electronic signature on this return creates personal criminal exposure if the declaration is knowingly false.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; negligent under-reporting triggers a 10% penalty, and unfair or fraudulent under-reporting triggers a 40% penalty. Unpaid tax accrues a late payment surcharge at approximately 0.022%-0.027% per day, equivalent to roughly 8%-10% per annum, until fully paid. Knowingly filing a false or fraudulent corporate tax return or causing false foreign withholding claims is criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, carrying imprisonment for up to five years and fines of up to five times the evaded tax, in addition to civil penalty surcharges and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident dividends are subject to 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, producing a combined statutory rate of 22% on gross dividend distributions; a lower rate may apply under an applicable double tax treaty if the recipient is the beneficial owner and a certified tax resident of the treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief in Korea, the Korean paying entity must submit, before or at the time of payment through HomeTax, a formal non-resident tax treaty reduction/exemption application together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority, a declaration that the foreign recipient is the beneficial owner, a confirmation that the recipient has no Korean permanent establishment to which the income is attributable, and supporting transaction contracts. The NTS reviews the actual substance of the recipient and may deny relief for conduit or shell companies. If relief is denied, the Korean payor must withhold the full 22% and the beneficial owner may pursue a refund under the tax treaty by filing a reimbursement claim with supporting evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest paid by a Korean company to a non-resident is also 20% national tax plus 2% local surtax, namely 22% absent treaty. Most Korean income tax treaties reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and asset character; the treaty rate is available only if the foreign recipient files the required TRC, beneficial ownership declaration and PE confirmation before remittance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when aggregate overseas related-party transactions reach KRW 5 billion or more in a business year; Master File is mandatory when the Korean taxpayer has related-party transactions of KRW 50 billion or more and global revenue of KRW 100 billion or more; CbC Report is required for ultimate parent groups with consolidated group revenue of KRW 2 trillion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain an enumerated Economic Substance Regulations regime similar to the UAE, but the NTS applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the Korean General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the OECD BEPS/MLI minimum standards and the beneficial ownership test to recharacterize shell structures. For a commercial 3D animation company, the core income-generating activities consist of script and character development, digital asset creation, VFX rendering infrastructure, licensing negotiation, IP management and post-production supervision; these activities must be conducted in Korea by substantive employees and assets to avoid attribution of income to an offshore principal and to preserve treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting overseas 3D animation licensing royalties, VFX service revenue or content distribution income received through Wise B2B, SWIFT wires or third-party digital payment accounts; issuing false invoices from non-resident subcontractors to increase production costs; making false declarations in the annual corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Offenses Act: imprisonment with labor for up to five years or a fine not exceeding five times the amount of tax evaded; civil additional tax of 40% of the under-reported tax, plus daily late payment surcharges; immediate criminal referral to the prosecution service and forfeiture of the proceeds of the concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean corporate veil may be pierced where the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a mere instrument to evade tax; directors who participated in the fraudulent return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties from personal assets; directors face asset attachment, travel bans and immigration blacklisting for tax arrears exceeding KRW 50 million, and criminal imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling animation IP licenses, 3D modeling services and VFX deliverables to a related offshore distributor at below arm's length prices; paying inflated royalties, management fees or loan interest to a related foreign shareholder without actual services; failing to prepare or submit the Local File, Master File or CbC Report when the statutory Korean Won thresholds are crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Coordination Act articles 4 through 6 give the NTS authority to re-determine the arm's length price and assess corporate tax on the adjusted income; failure to preserve or submit contemporaneous TP documentation can trigger an additional penalty of 30% of the tax understatement, along with late payment surcharges of approximately 0.022%-0.027% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false transfer pricing documentation is treated as a co-participant in tax evasion and may be jointly and severally liable for the entire tax shortfall, penalties and interest; personal bank accounts, real property and dividends may be seized, the director may be prohibited from leaving Korea, and criminal imprisonment may be imposed where the TP mispricing was designed solely to strip Korean profits offshore.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Default and Treaty or AML Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, royalties or interest to non-resident shareholders or related parties without withholding the statutory 22% combined national and local tax; using shell companies in treaty jurisdictions to claim a reduced DTA rate without economic substance; routing payments through multiple foreign jurisdictions or digital payment rails to disguise the true beneficial owner and avoid NTS withholding detection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean payor as withholding agent is liable for the uncollected WHT plus an additional penalty of 10%-20% for failure to withhold and remit; abusive DTA claims are recharacterized under general anti-avoidance rules and BEPS/MLI provisions; the false use of treaty relief constitutes fraud and triggers criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act together with Anti-Money Laundering referrals for structured cross-border wires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and corporate officers of the Korean withholding agent bear personal civil and criminal liability if they knowingly authorize non-resident payments without WHT; the corporate veil is pierced for improper use of the entity, making the director jointly and severally liable for the unpaid WHT, local surtax and penalties; directors may face personal asset execution, travel bans, blacklisting by Korean tax and immigration authorities, and imprisonment for the fraudulent non-compliance.
